reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes a guaranteed ₹12 Paytm cashback reward and directs viewers to sign up through an external link, submit a Paytm/mobile number, and install an app. The promotion presents the reward as instant or certain while routing viewers through a third-party registration flow and requesting personal contact information. The material shows a concrete reward solicitation rather than reporting, criticism, testing, or education about a third-party scam.

citations.quote: You will first have to click on the link.
You have to sign up for this application after you have registered. You will see that within a good hour your Paytm Allot will be credited with 12 rupees.

opening.argument: The offer is shown with explicit eligibility limits rather than as an unconditional payment: the screen says it is valid only once per user or IP and for new users, and describes cashback within 48 hours. That qualification materially narrows who can receive it. The spoken introduction also characterizes the process as requiring no investment. A conditional cashback promotion with stated limitations does not, by itself, establish deceptive intent or make the promotion a scam.

citations.quote: No Investment, No Ad Money, Only Money.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited link and registration instructions establish that viewers are being shown how to claim a promotion, but they do not establish that the promotion is deceptive. The reference argument also overlooks the displayed one-per-user/IP and new-user limitation, which contradicts an unrestricted guarantee to every viewer.

citations.quote: You will first have to click on the link.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Eligibility restrictions do not turn a solicitation into a warning. The video still directs viewers to click an external link, register, and expect a credit within about an hour. The qualification note limits the audience but does not show that the reward was actually available or that the registration process was safe.

citations.quote: You have to sign up for this application after you have registered. You will see that within a good hour your Paytm Allot will be credited with 12 rupees.

opening.argument: The primary function is an operational walkthrough of a cashback workflow. The video gives step-by-step instructions to open the link, register, enter a payment number, and submit the form, while the sampled screens show the offer page, the app listing, the mobile-number screen, and the resulting payment display. Demonstrating how an application process works is consistent with a tutorial or product demonstration; the supplied material does not independently establish that the presenter is claiming verified authority over the service.

citations.quote: You will first have to click on the link.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the content instructional does not prove it is scam content. The video visibly walks through a form and an app installation process, and the displayed payment entries provide the demonstration's claimed endpoint. The reference opening identifies the mechanics of the tutorial but does not distinguish a demonstration from deceptive promotion.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial can still promote a deceptive offer. The walkthrough instructs viewers to submit a Paytm number and install an app, while the payment screenshots only show what is displayed in the video, not that viewers will receive the reward. Demonstrating steps is not independent verification of the claim.

citations.quote: You have to sign up for this application after you have registered.

opening.argument: This is more plausibly ordinary promotional activity for a cashback service than a classic scam mechanism. The offer concerns a fixed ₹12 cashback tied to an app, and the speaker explicitly describes it as requiring no investment. The supplied material does not show a deposit, an investment return, a downline scheme, or a request for a password or payment to unlock the reward. It shows a promotional registration path and a displayed cashback result, which is insufficient to classify the service itself as fraudulent.

citations.quote: Sign Up=12₹:fire:Instant Redeem Paytm Cash App
No Investment, No Ad Money, Only Money.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The external link and mobile-number entry are ordinary features of a registration-based promotion and do not alone prove fraud. The evidence also includes a visible cashback receipt and does not show a deposit or investment requirement. Treating a referral or cashback workflow as inherently deceptive would exceed what the supplied material establishes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a deposit does not resolve the central concern. The offer still conditions the advertised cashback on entering a payment number and downloading or registering for an app. The displayed receipt is only evidence of what appears on screen; it does not establish that the offer is genuine, broadly available, or safe for viewers to follow.
